metadata.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: every DSH session becomes a Telegram forum topic, mirrored both ways, with approvals, questions, commands, files and voice
metadata.name: dsh-tg-bridge

paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness plugin: every DSH session becomes a Telegram forum topic, mirrored both ways, with
approvals, questions, commands, files and voice
# DSH Telegram bridge
English | Русский

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH)
plugin that gives every DSH session its own topic in a Telegram forum group

.
You can follow and drive a session from DSH or from Telegram; both sides see
the same conversation

You can follow and drive a session from DSH or from Telegram; both sides see
the same conversation.

- **One session, one topic.** Each root session gets a topic named
`workspace · session title`. It i

s renamed when DSH titles the session,
closed when you archive it, and reopened when you restore it.

- **Both directions.** Messages you type in DSH appear in the topic, with
their pictures as photos

(several as an album). Text,
photos, files and voice messages you send in the topic go into the sess

ion
exactly like a message typed in the DSH composer.
- **Agent output.** Answers stream live into o

ne message that is edited as the
model writes. Tool calls are collapsed into one expandable block pe

r run of
tools. Long answers arrive as `answer.md`; images the agent embeds or
presents arrive as ph

otos. While the agent works the topic shows "typing…";
when a turn ends, a notifying `✅ Done` line a

rrives.
- **Subagents.** Subagents never create topics. Each one shows as a single
line in its paren

t's topic: "working, waiting for result ⏳", then
"done ✅" (or failed ❌ / cancelled ⏹).
- **Approvals

and questions.** Approval requests and `ask_user_question`
prompts arrive with inline buttons. Tele

gram and the DSH GUI race: whichever
answers first wins, and the prompt on the other side is withdra

wn; a
question answered in DSH shows the chosen answer in the topic. Approvals,
questions and the en

d-of-turn line mention (@) whoever sent the request
from Telegram, or the first allowed user for req

uests typed in DSH.
- **Commands.** `/stop`, `/status`, `/diff`, `/compact`, `/model`,
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with the plugin manager (desktop app or `dsh web`).
- Node.js 22 or newer (the on

e DSH runs on).
- A Telegram bot from @BotFather.
- A Telegram supergroup with **Topics** enabled.
-
Optional: `ffmpeg` for voice messages.
## Install

1. In DSH open **Plugins → Add plugin** and enter one of:
- `github:Nergous/dsh-tg-bridge` (latest f

rom GitHub), or
- an absolute path to a local clone, for example `/home/me/projects/dsh-tg-bridge`.
2. Choose **Enable now**, then open **Plugins → Telegram bridge**.

The plugin has no build step and no dependencies. After changing host code
(`index.js`, `lib/`) rest
art DSH; `client.js` reloads in the open page.
## Set up

1. **Bot token.** Create a bot with @BotFather (`/newbot`), paste the token on
the settings page and

press **Save token**. The token is stored in DSH
credentials (`DSH_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`), never in c

onfiguration files. An
environment variable of the same name also works.
2. **Group.** Create a grou

p, open its settings and enable **Topics**. Add
the bot and make it an administrator with **Manage t

opics** and
**Pin messages**.
3. **Bind.** Press **Get bind code** and send `/bind <code>` in the gr

oup
within 10 minutes. The group is saved, and you are added to the allowed
users. Add more Telegram

user ids on the settings page if others should be
able to write to sessions. Messages from anyone e

lse, from bots and from
anonymous admins are ignored.
4. Press **Test connection**. It checks the to

ken, the group, Topics, and the
bot's rights.
5. Write something in any DSH session. Its topic appea

Topics, and the
bot's rights.
5. Write something in any DSH session. Its topic appears in the group.

Only one process may poll a bot. If DSH desktop and `dsh web` run at the same
time with this plugin,

Telegram answers `409 Conflict`; use one of them, or a
second bot.
## Limitations

- Topics are not backfilled: a topic shows the session from the moment it was
created.
- `/sessions`

lists the 15 most recent sessions; older ones get a topic when
you continue them in DSH.
- `/model`

uses DSH's model switch, which also changes the default model for
new sessions.
- DSH has no sessio

d out in Telegram can only be answered in DSH.
- One bot per running DSH process (see `409 Conflict`

Telegram can only be answered in DSH.
- One bot per running DSH process (see `409 Conflict` above).
## How it works
The plugin runs inside the DSH host process.

- It listens to DSH session events (`session/event`, `agent/assistant-stream`,
`subagent/start`, `su

bagent/end`) and sends Telegram messages through one
rate-limited queue per group. Streaming edits a

re coalesced so a busy group
gets fewer, larger edits instead of a backlog. Messages that are not sa

fe to
repeat are retried only when Telegram certainly did not receive them.
- Input from Telegram go

es through `sessionController.prompt`, the method the
DSH composer uses. A cold session is resumed w

ith its preset and model.
- Approvals and questions hook the `approval/request` and
`user-questions/

request` waterfalls before the GUI and race both answers.
The DSH GUI shows the prompt at once; Tele

gram never delays it.
- Root sessions are told apart from subagents by the session header
(`origin:

'subagent'`). Subagent approvals are shown in the root topic.
- The session-to-topic map (with each

session's last Telegram requester), the
polling offset and the names of allowed users (for mentions)

are stored in a
DSH storage domain (`~/.dsh/storages/telegram_bridge.json`).
- Pictures of DSH mess

ages are read back from DSH attachment storage
(`attachments` service).
## Security

- Only the bound group and the allowed user ids are served. Everything else is
ignored, including bu

tton presses, bots and anonymous admins.
- The bot token is kept in DSH credentials and never writte

n to logs, errors,
configuration, or the storage domain. The settings routes cannot change the
crede

ntial name or the Bot API URL.
- Settings routes use DSH's own authentication.
- Anyone who can writ

e in the group as an allowed user can run commands in
your sessions with the sessions' permissions.
Keep the group private.
See SECURITY.md to report a vulnerability.
